answer: Admission runs on serial judged work. An island joins identities whose work receipts resolve to the same audited income beneficiary; delta keeps its lifetime admission tally. Each epoch mints at most one nontransferable nadir to it, only for client-accepted work. Admitting identity \(k\) burns \(2k-1\) nadir earned after the latest join. One identity costs 1 accepted-work epoch; ten cost 100 serial epochs, the tenth 19. Pre-farmed credits die on joining, fresh wallets cannot change the beneficiary, and an unrelated beneficiary starts at 1.
